newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED CRUISE TO COMFORTABLE WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED CRUISE TO COMFORTABLE WIN.

text.p: English champions Manchester United cruised to a comfortable 2-0 European Cup win over Rapid Vienna of Austria on Wednesday with first half goals from Ole Solskjaer and David Beckham.

The English side, outclassed in their opening Champions' League Group C match against Juventus two weeks ago, enjoyed almost total domination in the opening period against the lacklustre Austrians but eased up after going two goals clear.
Norwegian Solskjaer opened the scoring in the 20th minute when he slid in a low right wing cross from Roy Keane at the far post.

Seven minutes later Beckham made it two when he took advantage of a poor back pass by Krzystof Ratajczyk, scoring on his second attempt after his first shot rebounded off keeper Michael Konsel's legs.
Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson recognised that his team had eased up after the interval but still pronounced himself satisfied.
"They threatened more down the right-hand side after the break," he said. "We maybe dropped the tempo a little when confronted with that problem and we should have kept possession more.
"But, other than that, I thought we maintained a good discipline, we weren't going to lose it and, like all games of football, you can't dominate for 90 minutes.
"We did for maybe an hour but in the last part of the match they did come into it a little bit. I'm satisfied, though. It is a good result and a good performance."

Manchester United: 1-Peter Schmeichel; 2-Gary Neville, 3-Denis Irwin, 5-Ronny Johnsen (4-David May 19th), 6-Gary Pallister, 7-Eric Cantona, 10-David Beckham, 11-Ryan Giggs, 15-Karel Poborsky (8-Nicky Butt 79th), 16-Roy Keane, 20-Ole Solskjaer (9-Andy Cole 75th).

Rapid Vienna: 1-Michael Konsel; 4-Trifon Ivanov, 5-Peter Schoettel, 6-Peter Stoeger (8-Zoran Barisic 63rd), 10-Dietmar Kuehbauer, 11-Christian Prosenik, 15-Andrzej Lesiak, 16-Krzystof Ratajczyk, 17-Rene Wagner (7-Christian Stumpf 63rd), 19-Thomas Zingler (2-Prvoslav Jovanovic 72nd), 20-Andreas Heraf.
